title: Simulation-trained network locates a physical magnetic resonator
summary: A convolutional-transformer regressor trained on simulated signals with measured noise located a physical magneto-mechanical resonator on a robot-positioned grid. Across repeated static recordings, median position error was 7.26 millimeters and the 95th percentile was 23.7 millimeters. This validates a specific laboratory readout under fixed-orientation conditions, without demonstrating clinical tracking.
organization: Hamburg University of Technology; University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf; Fraunhofer IMTE

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, signal/data/model Methods, robot-reference experiment, evaluation Results and limitations

evidence.tested: A model trained on 100000 simulated signals was tested on physical recordings at75 grid positions,25 frames each, against robot positions.
evidence.unknown: One resonator and fixed orientation, repeated static frames and one coil system limit generalization. Frame-level bootstrap uncertainty is not independent hardware replication. Errors were greater near the coil surface; normalized inputs can lose information there. No moving-device clinical test, outcome benefit or general parameter-estimation claim was established.
evidence.ai_role: The learned inverse mapping estimates three-dimensional position directly from measured multichannel time signals, enabling the reported robot-reference localization evaluation.
